NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI accelerator value chain, acting as a fabless semiconductor designer that relies critically on TSMC for cutting-edge chip fabrication and SK Hynix/Micron for scarce HBM memory, creating concentrated upstream dependencies. On the downstream side, NVIDIA's revenue is heavily driven by a small group of hyperscalers and cloud providers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) that are rapidly scaling AI infrastructure buildouts, giving NVIDIA extraordinary pricing power but also significant customer concentration risk.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting primarily as a design-and-brand house that outsources manufacturing to a network of Asian suppliers — most critically TSMC for chips and Samsung/LG for displays — while distributing finished products through carriers, major retailers, and its own direct channels worldwide. Its increasingly significant Services segment creates a parallel downstream dependency on platform partners like Google, app developers, and content providers, making Apple both a hardware supply chain orchestrator and a digital platform gatekeeper.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at a critical mid-point in the semiconductor supply chain, heavily dependent on a small number of specialized equipment manufacturers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX) for its capital-intensive fab operations, giving those suppliers significant pricing power. On the demand side, Micron is increasingly driven by AI infrastructure buildout — particularly HBM sales to NVIDIA — alongside stable consumption from hyperscalers and mobile OEMs, making its revenue highly cyclical yet strategically essential to the global technology ecosystem.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM sits at the intellectual property layer of the global semiconductor ecosystem, licensing CPU, GPU, and system IP to virtually every major chipmaker rather than manufacturing silicon itself, making its upstream dependencies primarily EDA software vendors and cloud infrastructure providers. Its downstream reach is extraordinarily broad — spanning mobile, cloud, automotive, and IoT — with royalties and licensing fees tied to billions of ARM-based chips shipped annually by customers like Apple, Qualcomm, Amazon, and MediaTek.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology sits in the middle of the data infrastructure semiconductor value chain, acting as a fabless chip designer that relies heavily on TSMC for advanced-node manufacturing while serving hyperscale cloud providers, networking OEMs, and storage companies with custom ASICs, Ethernet, and storage silicon. Its strategic pivot toward AI-driven custom silicon for major cloud customers (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) has made hyperscaler demand the dominant revenue driver, while its upstream dependency on TSMC's leading-edge nodes represents a critical concentration risk.
